**Australian Wildlife Field Surveyors (AWFS)**

**Status: Current administrative record**

---

**1. CHARTER AND INCORPORATION RECORD**

**Document reference:** AWFS-C-001 (Certified copy held in safe, filing cabinet A, folder 1)
**Original charter date:** See certified extract below.
**Registered office:** 14 Wattle Lane, Taralga, NSW 2580 (current; relocated from 7 Binya Street, Goulburn, in 2006).
**Constitution:** Adopted at the inaugural general meeting; last consolidated version dated 12 March 2019. Amendments to the Objects clause were approved by special resolution on 5 November 2021 and registered with the Australian Charities and Not-for-profits Commission (ACNC) on 2 December 2021.
**Incorporation type:** Incorporated association under the Associations Incorporation Act 2009 (NSW), with charity endorsement.

**Charter extract (certified):**
"Australian Wildlife Field Surveyors founded_year 1998 year. Record status: current." This entry is recorded in the certified copy of the charter, which remains the current controlling document for the organisation's establishment date. The charter was signed by the three founding members and witnessed by a Justice of the Peace.

---

**2. MINUTES – INAUGURAL GENERAL MEETING**

**Date of meeting:** 14 March 1998
**Location:** Taralga Community Hall, Taralga, NSW
**Chair:** M. Chen (interim)
**Secretary:** P. Okafor (interim)
**In attendance:** 11 persons (full list in attendance sheet, ref AWFS-M-1998-01-att)

**Resolutions passed:**
1. That the organisation be named "Australian Wildlife Field Surveyors" and that the name be adopted for all official purposes.
2. That the draft constitution, as circulated, be adopted.
3. That the office of the organisation be located in the Goulburn–Taralga district.
4. That the membership fee for the first year be set at $25 for individuals and $40 for organisations.
5. That the Committee of Management be elected, consisting of Chair, Secretary, Treasurer, and four ordinary members.

**Elected officers (inaugural):**
- Chair: M. Chen
- Secretary: P. Okafor
- Treasurer: J. Whitfield
- Ordinary members: R. Alvarez, S. Nguyen, T. Brown, K. Patel

**Other business:** Discussion concerning the purchase of a second-hand laptop computer and a tape recorder for field notes. It was agreed that the Treasurer would investigate costs.

**Meeting closed:** 5:10 pm.

**Signed:** P. Okafor (Secretary, 1998)
**Certified as true extract:** 3 April 1998.

---

**3. REGISTER OF FOUNDING MEMBERS**

*Note: The register has been maintained continuously since establishment. Founding members are those who signed the charter at the inaugural meeting. Status codes: F = Founding, C = Current, R = Resigned, D = Deceased.*

**Notes to the Register:**

1. The Northern Territory Field Station was established following a decision of the Committee of Management at its meeting of 8 November 2003 (Minute 03/47). The then Secretary, P. **STAFF REGISTER AND EMPLOYMENT RECORDS**
**PART 3: CONTRACTS AND ROLE ASSIGNMENTS (2009–2014)**

The following section records appointments and role assignments made between 1 January 2009 and 31 December 2014. Entries are drawn from original staff contracts, offer letters, and the minutes of the Committee of Management. Where a contract has been varied, the variation is noted in the margin. All entries have been verified against the personnel files held by the Secretariat.

---

**3.1 Appointments, 2009**

**09/001 – Dr. Emily Carter**
Appointed as a member of the scientific staff with effect from 2 March 2009. The staff contract lists Dr. Emily Carter's role as Senior Ecologist. Record status: current. Dr. Carter holds a Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Melbourne and had previously served as a research fellow with the Arid Lands Research Group. Her appointment followed a recommendation of the Scientific Advisory Committee (Minute 08/112) and was approved by the Committee of Management at its meeting of 19 January 2009 (Minute 09/03). The contract is for an initial term of three years, with provision for renewal by mutual consent.

**09/002 – Mr. Daniel Osei**
Appointed as Field Research Assistant with effect from 6 April 2009. Mr. Osei transferred from the Northern Territory Field Station, where he had been employed on a casual basis since 2007. His duties include the maintenance of survey equipment and assistance with the capture and handling of small mammals. The contract was renewed in 2012 and again in 2015.

**09/003 – Ms. Priya Raghavan**
Appointed as Administrative Officer (part-time, 0.6 FTE) with effect from 1 July 2009. Ms. Raghavan had previously been employed by the Alice Springs Town Council. Her responsibilities include the management of the station bookkeeping and the coordination of volunteer visits. The position was made full-time in 2013.

---

**3.2 Appointments, 2010**

**10/001 – Dr. Thomas Whitfield**
Appointed as Research Associate with effect from 11 January 2010. Dr. Whitfield was engaged to lead the organisation's study of the greater bilby in the Tanami Desert. The appointment was funded by a grant from the Commonwealth Government under the Caring for our Country program. Dr. Whitfield's contract ended on 30 June 2013, and he did not seek renewal.

**10/002 – Mr. James Okafor**
Appointed as Station Hand (casual) with effect from 15 February 2010. Mr. Okafor is the son of the former Secretary, P. Okafor, and was engaged to assist with general maintenance at the Alice Springs property. The appointment was made on the recommendation of the Station Manager. Mr. Okafor's casual engagement continued until 2016, when he resigned to take up a position with the Parks and Wildlife Commission.

**10/003 – Ms. Laura Chen**
Appointed as Volunteer Coordinator with effect from 1 September 2010. Ms. Chen had previously served as a volunteer on several of the organisation's surveys and was known to the Committee through her work with the Friends of the Desert Parks group. Her duties include the recruitment, training, and supervision of volunteers, as well as the maintenance of the volunteer register. The position was established following a review of the organisation's volunteer program (Minute 10/28).

---

**3.3 Appointments, 2011**

**11/001 – Dr. Sarah Lindqvist**
Appointed as Senior Ecologist (second position) with effect from 3 January 2011. Dr. Lindqvist was engaged to lead the organisation's program of research into the ecology of the thorny devil. The appointment was made possible by a bequest from the estate of the late Mr. Harold Finch, a long-standing member of the organisation. Dr. Lindqvist's contract was renewed in 2014 and again in 2017.
**3.4 Appointments, 2012**

**12/001 – Mr. Tom O'Reilly**
Appointed as Field Technician with effect from 9 January 2012. Mr. O'Reilly was engaged to support the organisation's field programs, with particular responsibility for the maintenance and deployment of camera traps, the servicing of remote weather stations, and the collection of vegetation survey data. He had previously worked for two seasons as a volunteer on the organisation's bilby monitoring program in the Tanami, and was known to the Committee through his work with the Central Land Council. The appointment was made on the recommendation of Dr. Whitfield, who had supervised Mr. O'Reilly during the 2011 field season.

Mr. O'Reilly's duties have expanded over time to include the training of volunteer field assistants in the use of GPS equipment and the basic identification of threatened species habitat. He is also responsible for the organisation's field equipment register, a task he assumed in 2015 following a review of asset management (Minute 15/12).

As part of the conditions of his employment, Mr. O'Reilly was required to hold a current First Aid Certificate. At the time of his appointment he held a certificate that had been issued in 2009, and he has maintained his certification continuously since then. His personnel file shows that he has completed refresher training on a regular basis. Tom O'Reilly's personnel file shows his certification as First Aid Certificate. Record status: current. This certification is current and is recorded as such in the organisation's training register. A copy of the certificate is held on file (see Appendix 4, Item 12/001-A).

Mr. O'Reilly has also undertaken a number of additional training courses during his employment, including:
- Remote area first aid (2014, 2017, 2020)
- Four-wheel drive operation and recovery (2013, 2018)
- Basic drone operation for aerial survey (2016)
- Chemical handling and application (2015)
- Defensive driving (2012)

These additional qualifications are noted in his training record but do not form part of his conditions of employment. The Committee notes that the organisation does not currently require drone operation certification for field staff, although this may be reviewed in light of the increasing use of drones in survey work.

Mr. O'Reilly's appointment was made permanent in July 2014 (Minute 14/23). He remains in the organisation's employ as at the date of this record.

---

**12/002 – Ms. Priya Sharma**
Appointed as Administrative Assistant (part-time, 0.5 FTE) with effect from 2 April 2012. Ms. Sharma was engaged to provide administrative support to the Secretary and the Station Manager, with particular responsibility for the processing of permit applications and the maintenance of the organisation's correspondence register. The position was created to address an identified gap in administrative capacity following the departure of the previous assistant in late 2011. Ms. Sharma's appointment was made on the recommendation of the Secretary.

Ms. Sharma resigned in September 2014 to relocate to Perth for family reasons. Her position was filled by Ms. Emily Tran (see 14/017).

---

**12/003 – Mr. Daniel Fitzpatrick**
Appointed as Field Technician (casual) with effect from 1 October 2012. Mr. Fitzpatrick was engaged to assist with the organisation's spring survey program and was employed on a seasonal basis for the duration of that program. His engagement was extended on several occasions, and he worked for the organisation on a casual basis until 2015, when he was offered a permanent position with the Northern Territory Government. The Committee records its appreciation of Mr. Fitzpatrick's contribution to the organisation's survey work.
Ms. Chen holds a Bachelor of Science (Environmental Science) from the University of Western Australia (2009) and a Graduate Certificate in Community Engagement (2012). She was previously employed by the Shire of Halls Creek as a community development officer.

Ms. Chen resigned in December 2017 to relocate to Darwin for family reasons. Her position was not filled immediately; the Committee agreed at its December 2017 meeting to defer recruitment until the outcome of the organisation's strategic review was known (Minute 17/31).

---

**13/001 – Mr. David Okafor**
Appointed as Field Officer (full-time) with effect from 4 February 2013. Mr. Okafor was engaged to support the organisation's survey work in the southern region, and to assist with the development of the organisation's threatened species database. He holds a Bachelor of Science (Zoology) from the University of Adelaide (2010) and had previously worked for two seasons as a field assistant with the South Australian Department of Environment, Water and Natural Resources.

Mr. Okafor's appointment was made following the retirement of Mr. Alan Wright (see 11/004). The Committee noted at the time of appointment that Mr. Okafor had strong skills in data collection and record keeping, and it was agreed that he would support the Data Manager in the maintenance of the organisation's species observation records.

Mr. Okafor remains in the organisation's employ as at the date of this record.

---

The management records assign Sarah Mitchell the data governance role of Data Manager. Record status: current.

**13/002 – Ms. Hannah Lee**
Appointed as Seasonal Field Assistant (casual) with effect from 1 March 2013, for the duration of the autumn survey program. Ms. Lee was engaged to assist with the organisation's waterbird surveys on the Ord River system. She had recently completed a Bachelor of Science (Wildlife Conservation) at Charles Darwin University and was seeking field experience prior to undertaking further study.

Ms. Lee's engagement was extended to cover the spring survey program in 2013, and she worked for the organisation on a casual basis until May 2014, when she resigned to commence a Master of Science (Wildlife Management) at the University of New England. The Committee records its appreciation of Ms. Lee's contribution.

---

**13/003 – Mr. James Nguyen**
Appointed as Station Manager with effect from 1 June 2013. Mr. Nguyen was engaged to manage the day-to-day operations of the organisation's field station near Kununurra, including the maintenance of vehicles, equipment, and the station buildings, and the supervision of field staff during their periods of residence at the station.

Mr. Nguyen had previously worked for the Northern Territory Parks and Wildlife Commission for eleven years, principally in the management of remote park facilities. He holds a Certificate III in Conservation and Land Management (2008) and a Certificate IV in Leadership and Management (2012).

Mr. Nguyen's appointment was made on the recommendation of the Secretary and the then-President, following a competitive recruitment process. The Committee noted at the time of appointment that Mr. Nguyen had indicated a strong interest in the organisation's data governance arrangements, and it was agreed that he would work closely with the Data Manager to ensure that field data were captured and stored in accordance with the organisation's protocols.

Mr. Nguyen remains in the organisation's employ as at the date of this record. His current role description, last reviewed in July 2022, includes responsibility for the oversight of the station's radio communications and the maintenance of the station's weather station equipment.
**13/004 – Dr. Rachel Green**
Engaged as a consultant veterinarian with effect from 1 September 2013. Dr. Green was appointed to provide veterinary oversight for the organisation's wildlife rehabilitation and field health programs, including the assessment of animals brought into care following vehicle strikes, dog attacks, and other incidents reported to the organisation's Kununurra office.

Dr. Green holds a Bachelor of Veterinary Science from the University of Queensland (2007) and had previously worked for three years with a private mixed practice in Townsville, where she developed an interest in native fauna. She had also volunteered with the Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service on their flying-fox care program during her final year of study. At the time of her engagement, Dr. Green was completing a Graduate Certificate in Wildlife and Zoo Animal Health at Murdoch University, which she finished in December 2013.

The HR records indicate Dr. Rachel Green's specialization is Wildlife Veterinarian. Record status: current. This specialisation is current and is recorded against her staff profile as at the date of this record. Her engagement letter of 12 August 2013 describes her role as providing "veterinary services for the treatment, rehabilitation, and release of native wildlife, and advice to field staff on animal health and welfare matters."

Dr. Green's appointment was made on the recommendation of the then-President and the Treasurer, following discussion with the Department of Parks and Wildlife regarding the increasing number of wildlife care cases in the East Kimberley region. The Committee approved a part-time consultancy arrangement of two days per week, with provision for additional days during peak seasons such as the post-flood period and the dry season fruit bat breeding cycle.

During 2014, Dr. Green coordinated the organisation's response to a cluster of avian botulism cases at Lake Argyle, working with the Waterbird Survey Coordinator to assess and treat affected waterbirds. Her report on that outbreak, dated 14 November 2014, is held on file and was presented to the Committee at its December 2014 meeting.

Dr. Green remains engaged by the organisation as at the date of this record. Her current consultancy agreement, last renewed in February 2023, continues to list her specialisation as Wildlife Veterinarian, and she is the organisation's principal contact for veterinary matters.

---

**13/005 – Mr. Daniel Okafor**
Appointed as Field Ecologist with effect from 1 October 2013. Mr. Okafor was engaged to lead the vegetation monitoring program and to provide botanical expertise for the organisation's land management projects across the Keep River and Ord River catchments.

Mr. Okafor holds a Bachelor of Science (Environmental Science) from the University of Western Australia (2008) and a Master of Science (Ecology) from the same institution (2011). His master's research examined fire regimes and their effect on spinifex grasslands in the Pilbara, and he had subsequently worked for two years as a seasonal field officer with the Rangelands NRM Coordinating Group in Geraldton.

Mr. Okafor's appointment was made following a competitive process in which the Committee interviewed three shortlisted candidates. The selection panel noted Mr. Okafor's strong quantitative skills and his familiarity with the organisation's survey methods, which he had used during a volunteer stint on the 2012 vegetation survey. His role description includes responsibility for the supervision of volunteer field assistants and the maintenance of the herbarium reference collection at the Kununurra office.

Mr. Okafor resigned in March 2016 to take up a position with the Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions in Perth. The Committee records its thanks for his contribution, particularly his work on the 2015 fire management plan and his training of two local ranger groups in vegetation survey techniques.
**ORGANISATIONAL HISTORY AND FOUNDING RECORDS – ADDENDUM 2016–2018**

*The following entries supplement the main chronological record. They are maintained by the Secretariat and verified against Committee minutes, contracts, and correspondence held on file.*

---

**2016 – Administrative and Program Developments**

**16/001 – Resignation of Mr. Daniel Okafor (recorded March 2016)**
The Committee accepted Mr. Okafor's resignation with regret at its March 2016 meeting. His final day of service was 31 March 2016. A letter of thanks was issued on 4 April 2016, acknowledging his contribution to the 2015 fire management plan and his training of two local ranger groups in vegetation survey techniques. His position was advertised in April 2016.

**16/002 – Appointment of Ms. Priya Sharma as Field Ecologist**
Following a recruitment process that concluded in May 2016, the Committee appointed Ms. Priya Sharma as Field Ecologist, with effect from 1 July 2016. Ms. Sharma holds a Bachelor of Science (Honours) in Botany from the University of Melbourne (2010) and a Doctor of Philosophy in Plant Ecology from the Australian National University (2015). Her doctoral research examined the effects of grazing exclusion on riparian vegetation in the Murray-Darling Basin.

Ms. Sharma previously worked as a research assistant with the Arthur Rylah Institute for Environmental Research, where she contributed to wetland vegetation assessments in northern Victoria. Her appointment was recommended by a panel chaired by the Vice-Chair, who noted her strong publication record and her experience with remote sensing techniques applicable to the organisation's monitoring programs.

Ms. Sharma's role description includes responsibility for the vegetation monitoring program, the supervision of volunteer field assistants, and the maintenance of the herbarium reference collection at the Kununurra office, succeeding Mr. Okafor in these duties.

**16/003 – Volunteer Program Expansion**
At its June 2016 meeting, the Committee approved an expansion of the volunteer field assistant program. The program had previously supported the annual vegetation survey and the waterbird health assessments. The expansion increased the number of volunteer placements from six to twelve per year, with a focus on involving local high school students in data collection activities. The first cohort under the expanded program commenced in July 2016.

**16/004 – Relocation of Office Records**
In August 2016, the organisation relocated its paper records from the previous storage facility in Kununurra to a new climate-controlled storage room at the main office. The move was completed on 19 August 2016. A complete inventory of transferred files was prepared by the Secretariat and is held in the current filing system. No records were reported lost or damaged during the move.

---

**2017 – Governance and Membership**

**17/001 – Committee Elections**
The 2017 Annual General Meeting was held on 21 October 2017. The following office bearers were elected for the 2017–2019 term:

- Chair: Mr. Geoffrey Thompson (re-elected)
- Vice-Chair: Ms. Helen Nguyen (re-elected)
- Treasurer: Mr. Robert Chen (newly elected, replacing Mr. Alan Foster who did not seek re-election)
- Secretary: Ms. Margaret Doyle (re-elected)

Mr. Foster was thanked for his six years of service as Treasurer, during which he oversaw the organisation's budget through the 2015 waterbird health response and the 2016 volunteer program expansion.

**17/002 – Membership Growth**
Membership numbers continued to grow steadily. As at 31 December 2016, the organisation had 214 financial members. By 31 December 2017, this figure had increased to 247. The growth was attributed to the volunteer program expansion and to increased public engagement activities, including the annual community bird survey held each September.
**2018 – Governance, Finances and Outreach**

**18/001 – Annual General Meeting and Committee Elections**
The 2018 Annual General Meeting was held on 20 October 2018. The following office bearers were elected for the 2018–2020 term:

- Chair: Mr. Geoffrey Thompson (re-elected)
- Vice-Chair: Ms. Helen Nguyen (re-elected)
- Treasurer: Mr. Robert Chen (re-elected)
- Secretary: Ms. Margaret Doyle (re-elected)

The meeting was attended by 62 members. A motion was passed to formally record the organisation's appreciation to the Shire for the continued use of the community hall for the AGM and other public events.

**18/002 – Membership Report**
As at 31 December 2017, the organisation had 247 financial members. By 31 December 2018, this figure had increased to 286. The Secretariat attributes the continued growth to the school holiday birdwatching workshops introduced in April 2018 and to the success of the September community bird survey, which recorded its highest participation to date with 94 volunteers.

**18/003 – Volunteer Program Update**
The volunteer field assistant program, expanded in 2016, continued to operate at full capacity during 2018. Twelve placements were filled across the vegetation survey and waterbird health assessments. The Committee noted with pleasure that three former volunteers from the 2017 cohort had enrolled in tertiary environmental science courses.

**18/004 – Community Bird Survey**
The annual community bird survey was held on 15 September 2018. A total of 94 volunteers participated, up from 71 in 2017. The survey covered the usual transects along the Ord River and the irrigation area. Preliminary results were presented to the Committee in November 2018. The final report was published in February 2019 and is available from the Secretariat upon request.

**18/005 – Funding Grant – Waterbird Habitat Restoration**
In March 2018, the organisation was awarded a grant of $45,000 from the State Government's Community Environment Fund. The grant was for a two-year project to restore and enhance waterbird habitat along a section of the Ord River. The project commenced in July 2018 with the engagement of a part-time project officer. The first planting season was completed in December 2018, with 2,400 seedlings of local riparian species planted. A progress report was submitted to the funding body in January 2019.

**18/006 – Partnership with Kimberley TAFE**
In August 2018, the organisation entered into a formal partnership with Kimberley TAFE. Under the agreement, TAFE students enrolled in the Certificate II in Conservation and Ecosystem Management would complete their work placement with the organisation. The first intake of four students commenced their placement in October 2018. The Committee noted that the partnership would provide additional capacity for the vegetation survey and would support the organisation's educational objectives.

**18/007 – Office Relocation of Field Equipment**
In November 2018, the organisation relocated its field equipment store from the old shed at the back of the main office to a new lockable container. The move was necessary because the old shed was no longer weatherproof. A full inventory of equipment was undertaken during the move. A small number of items, including two ageing mist nets and one pair of binoculars, were assessed as beyond repair and were disposed of with the approval of the Committee. The new storage container is located adjacent to the main office car park.

**18/008 – Revised Financial Procedures**
Following the 2018 audit, the Committee adopted a revised set of financial procedures. The changes were introduced to strengthen internal controls and to align with the updated requirements of the organisation's insurer. The key changes were:
**Organisational History and Founding Records (Continued)**

**18/009 – Appointment of New Treasurer**

In December 2018, the Committee appointed Mrs Helen Vickers as Treasurer, following the resignation of Mr Alan Pritchard who had held the position since 2015. Mr Pritchard stepped down due to increased work commitments and was thanked by the Committee for his service. Mrs Vickers had previously served as a Committee member from 2012 to 2016 and had experience in bookkeeping for a small business in Kununurra. The appointment was ratified at the Annual General Meeting held in February 2019. The new Treasurer's first task was to oversee the transition of the organisation's accounts to a new cloud-based accounting system, which was completed in March 2019.

**18/010 – Volunteer Recognition Program**

The Committee endorsed a Volunteer Recognition Program in November 2018, to acknowledge the contribution of the organisation's volunteer base. Under the program, volunteers who complete more than 50 hours of service in a calendar year receive a certificate of appreciation and a small gift. The first awards were presented at the end of year gathering in December 2018. A total of 12 volunteers qualified for the initial round of awards. The program has been well received and will continue on an annual basis.

**19/001 – Annual General Meeting and Committee Elections**

The Annual General Meeting was held on 16 February 2019 at the Kununurra Community Hall. The meeting was attended by 23 members. The following office bearers were elected for the 2019–2020 term:

- President: Mr David Chen (re-elected)
- Vice President: Ms Sarah Thompson (re-elected)
- Secretary: Ms Margaret O'Donnell (re-elected)
- Treasurer: Mrs Helen Vickers (newly appointed, as noted above)
- Committee members: Mr Peter Nguyen, Ms Julie Brown, Mr Robert Hayes, and Ms Fiona Gallagher

The meeting also endorsed the revised financial procedures adopted by the Committee in late 2018. The minutes of the meeting were circulated to members in March 2019 and are available from the Secretariat upon request.

**19/002 – Waterbird Habitat Restoration Project – Year Two**

The second year of the Waterbird Habitat Restoration Project commenced in July 2019. The part-time project officer, Mr Daniel Wong, continued in his role. The focus for Year Two was on weed control and supplementary planting. A total of 1,200 seedlings were planted in November 2019 to replace those that had not survived the first season. The project also included a community planting day in September 2019, which attracted 15 local volunteers. A final report was submitted to the funding body in January 2020. The report noted that the project had achieved its primary objectives, including the restoration of approximately 3.5 kilometres of riparian vegetation.

**19/003 – New Field Equipment Purchases**

In March 2019, the Committee approved the purchase of new field equipment using funds remaining from the waterbird habitat grant. The purchases included two new mist nets, a pair of binoculars, and a portable GPS unit. The total cost was $3,850. The equipment was purchased from a local supplier and was added to the inventory in April 2019. The new mist nets replaced the ageing nets that had been disposed of during the office relocation in November 2018.

**19/004 – Membership Changes**

The organisation recorded a net increase in membership during the 2018–2019 financial year. As at 30 June 2019, the organisation had 87 financial members, compared with 79 at the end of the previous year. The increase was attributed to the community planting day and the waterbird habitat project, which had raised the organisation's public profile. The membership subcommittee, led by Ms Julie Brown, continued to review the membership renewal process. A reminder system was introduced in August 2019, resulting in a higher rate of on-time renewals.
**2020 Committee Meeting Minutes – Summary of Actions**

**20/001 – Appointment of New Treasurer**

At the Annual General Meeting held in November 2019, the outgoing Treasurer, Mr Peter Thompson, indicated that he would not seek re-election due to personal commitments. The Committee accepted his resignation with thanks for his service over the preceding six years. Following a call for nominations, Ms Linda Carter was elected as Treasurer effective 1 January 2020. Ms Carter holds a Bachelor of Commerce and has served on the finance subcommittee since 2017. The handover of financial records was completed on 15 January 2020, and a review of the accounts by the independent auditor was scheduled for March 2020. The Committee recorded its appreciation for Mr Thompson's diligent management of the organisation's finances.

**20/002 – Review of the Constitution**

In February 2020, the Committee established a working group to review the organisation's constitution. The review was prompted by changes to the Associations Incorporation Act and by feedback from members regarding the clarity of the rules relating to proxy voting and the election of office bearers. The working group, chaired by Ms Julie Brown, was asked to report back to the Committee by June 2020. The terms of reference included a requirement to consult with members through a survey and to propose amendments for consideration at the next Annual General Meeting. The Committee noted that any changes to the constitution would require the approval of a two-thirds majority of members present at the AGM.

**20/003 – Woodland Bird Monitoring Program – Extension**

The Woodland Bird Monitoring Program, which had been running since 2017, was extended for a further two years following a successful funding application to a philanthropic trust. The extension, announced in March 2020, secured $18,000 to support the program through to June 2022. The program involves seasonal surveys at twelve fixed sites across the region. Volunteers conduct the surveys under the supervision of the program coordinator, Dr Sarah Mitchell. The data collected are used to track trends in woodland bird populations and to inform habitat management recommendations. The funding agreement requires the submission of interim progress reports in December 2020 and December 2021, with a final report due in August 2022.

**20/004 – Office Relocation – Finalisation of Lease**

The organisation completed the relocation of its office premises in November 2018. A short-term lease on the new premises was signed at that time. In April 2020, the Committee approved the signing of a new three-year lease for the same premises, with an option to renew for a further two years. The new lease commenced on 1 May 2020. The rental amount reflects a modest increase of 3% per annum over the term of the lease. The Committee considered alternatives, including sharing premises with another conservation group, but determined that the current location provided the best balance of cost, accessibility, and storage capacity for field equipment. The lease document is held by the Secretariat.

**20/005 – Wetland Rehabilitation Project – Community Engagement**

In May 2020, the organisation commenced a community engagement component of the Wetland Rehabilitation Project. The project, which is funded by a local government grant, aims to improve the condition of a degraded wetland on the outskirts of the town. The engagement component was designed to raise awareness of the project and to recruit volunteers for planting and weed control activities. A public information session was held on 23 May 2020 and was attended by 22 residents. A project sign was installed at the wetland entrance in June 2020. The engagement activities were coordinated by Mr Daniel Wong, who was employed part-time as the project officer. Mr Wong's contract was extended to December 2020 to cover this work.

Entries are numbered sequentially and cross-reference the minutes of the Committee of Management where relevant. Status codes: A = Active, S = Sold/Disposed, L = Leased, P = Pending, R = Retired. Where a title search or survey has been completed, the reference is noted in the Remarks column.*

| Item No. | Description | Interest | Status | Date of Acquisition | Remarks |

**Notes to the Register:**

1. The Northern Territory Field Station was established following a decision of the Committee of Management at its meeting of 8 November 2003 (Minute 03/47). The then Secretary, P. Okafor, was authorised to investigate suitable sites for a permanent base in central Australia, with a view to supporting long-term studies of arid-zone fauna.
2. The acquisition of the Alice Springs property was completed on 15 May 2004. The purchase price was $185,000, funded partly from accumulated reserves and partly from a grant provided by the Northern Territory Government under its Regional Environmental Program. The transfer was effected by the firm of Whitfield & Associates, Solicitors, of Goulburn.
3. It is recorded for the avoidance of doubt that the station is located in the town of Alice Springs and not at any other location in the Northern Territory. A search of the organisation's records confirms that no other property has been held in the Northern Territory, apart from the demountable unit referred to at P-004, which was situated on land leased from the Alice Springs Town Council and has since been removed.
4. The Committee has from time to time considered establishing a second field station in the Kimberley region of Western Australia, and also a small research hut near Oodnadatta. Neither proposal has proceeded beyond preliminary discussion. The minutes of the meeting of 12 September 2018 record that the Committee resolved to defer any such proposal until the financial position of the organisation permitted.

**STAFF REGISTER AND EMPLOYMENT RECORDS**
**PART 3: CONTRACTS AND ROLE ASSIGNMENTS (2009–2014)**

The following section records appointments and role assignments made between 1 January 2009 and 31 December 2014. Entries are drawn from original staff contracts, offer letters, and the minutes of the Committee of Management. Where a contract has been varied, the variation is noted in the margin. All entries have been verified against the personnel files held by the Secretariat.

---

**3.1 Appointments, 2009**

**09/001 – Dr. Emily Carter**
Appointed as a member of the scientific staff with effect from 2 March 2009. The staff contract lists Dr. Emily Carter's role as Senior Ecologist. Record status: current. Dr. Carter holds a Doctor of Philosophy from the University of Melbourne and had previously served as a research fellow with the Arid Lands Research Group. Her appointment followed a recommendation of the Scientific Advisory Committee (Minute 08/112) and was approved by the Committee of Management at its meeting of 19 January 2009 (Minute 09/03). The contract is for an initial term of three years, with provision for renewal by mutual consent.

**09/002 – Mr. Daniel Osei**
Appointed as Field Research Assistant with effect from 6 April 2009. Mr. Osei transferred from the Northern Territory Field Station, where he had been employed on a casual basis since 2007. His duties include the maintenance of survey equipment and assistance with the capture and handling of small mammals. The contract was renewed in 2012 and again in 2015.

**09/003 – Ms. Priya Raghavan**
Appointed as Administrative Officer (part-time, 0.6 FTE) with effect from 1 July 2009. Ms. Raghavan had previously been employed by the Alice Springs Town Council. Her responsibilities include the management of the station bookkeeping and the coordination of volunteer visits. The position was made full-time in 2013.

---

**3.2 Appointments, 2010**

**10/001 – Dr. Thomas Whitfield**
Appointed as Research Associate with effect from 11 January 2010. Dr. Whitfield was engaged to lead the organisation's study of the greater bilby in the Tanami Desert. The appointment was funded by a grant from the Commonwealth Government under the Caring for our Country program. Dr. Whitfield's contract ended on 30 June 2013, and he did not seek renewal.

**10/002 – Mr. James Okafor**
Appointed as Station Hand (casual) with effect from 15 February 2010. Mr. Okafor is the son of the former Secretary, P. Okafor, and was engaged to assist with general maintenance at the Alice Springs property. The appointment was made on the recommendation of the Station Manager. Mr. Okafor's casual engagement continued until 2016, when he resigned to take up a position with the Parks and Wildlife Commission.

**10/003 – Ms. Laura Chen**
Appointed as Volunteer Coordinator with effect from 1 September 2010. Ms. Chen had previously served as a volunteer on several of the organisation's surveys and was known to the Committee through her work with the Friends of the Desert Parks group. Her duties include the recruitment, training, and supervision of volunteers, as well as the maintenance of the volunteer register. The position was established following a review of the organisation's volunteer program (Minute 10/28).

---

**3.3 Appointments, 2011**

**11/001 – Dr. Sarah Lindqvist**
Appointed as Senior Ecologist (second position) with effect from 3 January 2011. Dr. Lindqvist was engaged to lead the organisation's program of research into the ecology of the thorny devil. The appointment was made possible by a bequest from the estate of the late Mr. Harold Finch, a long-standing member of the organisation. Dr. Lindqvist's contract was renewed in 2014 and again in 2017.

**3.4 Appointments, 2012**

**12/001 – Mr. Tom O'Reilly**
Appointed as Field Technician with effect from 9 January 2012. Mr. O'Reilly was engaged to support the organisation's field programs, with particular responsibility for the maintenance and deployment of camera traps, the servicing of remote weather stations, and the collection of vegetation survey data. He had previously worked for two seasons as a volunteer on the organisation's bilby monitoring program in the Tanami, and was known to the Committee through his work with the Central Land Council. The appointment was made on the recommendation of Dr. Whitfield, who had supervised Mr. O'Reilly during the 2011 field season.

Mr. O'Reilly's duties have expanded over time to include the training of volunteer field assistants in the use of GPS equipment and the basic identification of threatened species habitat. He is also responsible for the organisation's field equipment register, a task he assumed in 2015 following a review of asset management (Minute 15/12).

As part of the conditions of his employment, Mr. O'Reilly was required to hold a current First Aid Certificate. At the time of his appointment he held a certificate that had been issued in 2009, and he has maintained his certification continuously since then. His personnel file shows that he has completed refresher training on a regular basis. Tom O'Reilly's personnel file shows his certification as First Aid Certificate. Record status: current. This certification is current and is recorded as such in the organisation's training register. A copy of the certificate is held on file (see Appendix 4, Item 12/001-A).

Mr. O'Reilly has also undertaken a number of additional training courses during his employment, including:
- Remote area first aid (2014, 2017, 2020)
- Four-wheel drive operation and recovery (2013, 2018)
- Basic drone operation for aerial survey (2016)
- Chemical handling and application (2015)
- Defensive driving (2012)

These additional qualifications are noted in his training record but do not form part of his conditions of employment. The Committee notes that the organisation does not currently require drone operation certification for field staff, although this may be reviewed in light of the increasing use of drones in survey work.

Mr. O'Reilly's appointment was made permanent in July 2014 (Minute 14/23). He remains in the organisation's employ as at the date of this record.

---

**12/002 – Ms. Priya Sharma**
Appointed as Administrative Assistant (part-time, 0.5 FTE) with effect from 2 April 2012. Ms. Sharma was engaged to provide administrative support to the Secretary and the Station Manager, with particular responsibility for the processing of permit applications and the maintenance of the organisation's correspondence register. The position was created to address an identified gap in administrative capacity following the departure of the previous assistant in late 2011. Ms. Sharma's appointment was made on the recommendation of the Secretary.

Ms. Sharma resigned in September 2014 to relocate to Perth for family reasons. Her position was filled by Ms. Emily Tran (see 14/017).

---

**12/003 – Mr. Daniel Fitzpatrick**
Appointed as Field Technician (casual) with effect from 1 October 2012. Mr. Fitzpatrick was engaged to assist with the organisation's spring survey program and was employed on a seasonal basis for the duration of that program. His engagement was extended on several occasions, and he worked for the organisation on a casual basis until 2015, when he was offered a permanent position with the Northern Territory Government. **13/004 – Dr. Rachel Green**
Engaged as a consultant veterinarian with effect from 1 September 2013. Dr. Green was appointed to provide veterinary oversight for the organisation's wildlife rehabilitation and field health programs, including the assessment of animals brought into care following vehicle strikes, dog attacks, and other incidents reported to the organisation's Kununurra office.

Dr. Green holds a Bachelor of Veterinary Science from the University of Queensland (2007) and had previously worked for three years with a private mixed practice in Townsville, where she developed an interest in native fauna. She had also volunteered with the Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service on their flying-fox care program during her final year of study. At the time of her engagement, Dr. Green was completing a Graduate Certificate in Wildlife and Zoo Animal Health at Murdoch University, which she finished in December 2013.

The HR records indicate Dr. Rachel Green's specialization is Wildlife Veterinarian. Record status: current. This specialisation is current and is recorded against her staff profile as at the date of this record. Her engagement letter of 12 August 2013 describes her role as providing "veterinary services for the treatment, rehabilitation, and release of native wildlife, and advice to field staff on animal health and welfare matters."

Dr. Green's appointment was made on the recommendation of the then-President and the Treasurer, following discussion with the Department of Parks and Wildlife regarding the increasing number of wildlife care cases in the East Kimberley region. The Committee approved a part-time consultancy arrangement of two days per week, with provision for additional days during peak seasons such as the post-flood period and the dry season fruit bat breeding cycle.

During 2014, Dr. Green coordinated the organisation's response to a cluster of avian botulism cases at Lake Argyle, working with the Waterbird Survey Coordinator to assess and treat affected waterbirds. Her report on that outbreak, dated 14 November 2014, is held on file and was presented to the Committee at its December 2014 meeting.

Dr. Green remains engaged by the organisation as at the date of this record. Her current consultancy agreement, last renewed in February 2023, continues to list her specialisation as Wildlife Veterinarian, and she is the organisation's principal contact for veterinary matters.

---

**13/005 – Mr. Daniel Okafor**
Appointed as Field Ecologist with effect from 1 October 2013. Mr. Okafor was engaged to lead the vegetation monitoring program and to provide botanical expertise for the organisation's land management projects across the Keep River and Ord River catchments.

Mr. Okafor holds a Bachelor of Science (Environmental Science) from the University of Western Australia (2008) and a Master of Science (Ecology) from the same institution (2011). His master's research examined fire regimes and their effect on spinifex grasslands in the Pilbara, and he had subsequently worked for two years as a seasonal field officer with the Rangelands NRM Coordinating Group in Geraldton.

Mr. Okafor's appointment was made following a competitive process in which the Committee interviewed three shortlisted candidates. The selection panel noted Mr. Okafor's strong quantitative skills and his familiarity with the organisation's survey methods, which he had used during a volunteer stint on the 2012 vegetation survey. His role description includes responsibility for the supervision of volunteer field assistants and the maintenance of the herbarium reference collection at the Kununurra office.

Mr. Okafor resigned in March 2016 to take up a position with the Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions in Perth. The Committee records its thanks for his contribution, particularly his work on the 2015 fire management plan and his training of two local ranger groups in vegetation survey techniques.

**ORGANISATIONAL HISTORY AND FOUNDING RECORDS – ADDENDUM 2016–2018**

*The following entries supplement the main chronological record. They are maintained by the Secretariat and verified against Committee minutes, contracts, and correspondence held on file.*

---

**2016 – Administrative and Program Developments**

**16/001 – Resignation of Mr. Daniel Okafor (recorded March 2016)**
The Committee accepted Mr. Okafor's resignation with regret at its March 2016 meeting. His final day of service was 31 March 2016. A letter of thanks was issued on 4 April 2016, acknowledging his contribution to the 2015 fire management plan and his training of two local ranger groups in vegetation survey techniques. His position was advertised in April 2016.

**16/002 – Appointment of Ms. Priya Sharma as Field Ecologist**
Following a recruitment process that concluded in May 2016, the Committee appointed Ms. Priya Sharma as Field Ecologist, with effect from 1 July 2016. Ms. Sharma holds a Bachelor of Science (Honours) in Botany from the University of Melbourne (2010) and a Doctor of Philosophy in Plant Ecology from the Australian National University (2015). Her doctoral research examined the effects of grazing exclusion on riparian vegetation in the Murray-Darling Basin.

Ms. Sharma previously worked as a research assistant with the Arthur Rylah Institute for Environmental Research, where she contributed to wetland vegetation assessments in northern Victoria. Her appointment was recommended by a panel chaired by the Vice-Chair, who noted her strong publication record and her experience with remote sensing techniques applicable to the organisation's monitoring programs.

Ms. Sharma's role description includes responsibility for the vegetation monitoring program, the supervision of volunteer field assistants, and the maintenance of the herbarium reference collection at the Kununurra office, succeeding Mr. Okafor in these duties.

**16/003 – Volunteer Program Expansion**
At its June 2016 meeting, the Committee approved an expansion of the volunteer field assistant program. The program had previously supported the annual vegetation survey and the waterbird health assessments. The expansion increased the number of volunteer placements from six to twelve per year, with a focus on involving local high school students in data collection activities. The first cohort under the expanded program commenced in July 2016.

**16/004 – Relocation of Office Records**
In August 2016, the organisation relocated its paper records from the previous storage facility in Kununurra to a new climate-controlled storage room at the main office. The move was completed on 19 August 2016. A complete inventory of transferred files was prepared by the Secretariat and is held in the current filing system. No records were reported lost or damaged during the move.

---

**2017 – Governance and Membership**

**17/001 – Committee Elections**
The 2017 Annual General Meeting was held on 21 October 2017. The following office bearers were elected for the 2017–2019 term:

- Chair: Mr. Geoffrey Thompson (re-elected)
- Vice-Chair: Ms. Helen Nguyen (re-elected)
- Treasurer: Mr. Robert Chen (newly elected, replacing Mr. Alan Foster who did not seek re-election)
- Secretary: Ms. Margaret Doyle (re-elected)

Mr. Foster was thanked for his six years of service as Treasurer, during which he oversaw the organisation's budget through the 2015 waterbird health response and the 2016 volunteer program expansion.

**17/002 – Membership Growth**
Membership numbers continued to grow steadily. As at 31 December 2016, the organisation had 214 financial members. By 31 December 2017, this figure had increased to 247. The growth was attributed to the volunteer program expansion and to increased public engagement activities, including the annual community bird survey held each September.

**18/001 – Annual General Meeting and Committee Elections**
The 2018 Annual General Meeting was held on 20 October 2018. The following office bearers were elected for the 2018–2020 term:

- Chair: Mr. Geoffrey Thompson (re-elected)
- Vice-Chair: Ms. Helen Nguyen (re-elected)

The meeting was attended by 62 members. A motion was passed to formally record the organisation's appreciation to the Shire for the continued use of the community hall for the AGM and other public events.

**18/002 – Membership Report**
As at 31 December 2017, the organisation had 247 financial members. By 31 December 2018, this figure had increased to 286. The Secretariat attributes the continued growth to the school holiday birdwatching workshops introduced in April 2018 and to the success of the September community bird survey, which recorded its highest participation to date with 94 volunteers.

**18/003 – Volunteer Program Update**
The volunteer field assistant program, expanded in 2016, continued to operate at full capacity during 2018. Twelve placements were filled across the vegetation survey and waterbird health assessments. The Committee noted with pleasure that three former volunteers from the 2017 cohort had enrolled in tertiary environmental science courses.

**18/004 – Community Bird Survey**
The annual community bird survey was held on 15 September 2018. A total of 94 volunteers participated, up from 71 in 2017. The survey covered the usual transects along the Ord River and the irrigation area. Preliminary results were presented to the Committee in November 2018. The final report was published in February 2019 and is available from the Secretariat upon request.

**18/005 – Funding Grant – Waterbird Habitat Restoration**
In March 2018, the organisation was awarded a grant of $45,000 from the State Government's Community Environment Fund. The grant was for a two-year project to restore and enhance waterbird habitat along a section of the Ord River. The project commenced in July 2018 with the engagement of a part-time project officer. The first planting season was completed in December 2018, with 2,400 seedlings of local riparian species planted. A progress report was submitted to the funding body in January 2019.

In August 2018, the organisation entered into a formal partnership with Kimberley TAFE. Under the agreement, TAFE students enrolled in the Certificate II in Conservation and Ecosystem Management would complete their work placement with the organisation. The first intake of four students commenced their placement in October 2018. The Committee noted that the partnership would provide additional capacity for the vegetation survey and would support the organisation's educational objectives.

In November 2018, the organisation relocated its field equipment store from the old shed at the back of the main office to a new lockable container. The move was necessary because the old shed was no longer weatherproof. A full inventory of equipment was undertaken during the move. The new storage container is located adjacent to the main office car park.

**18/009 – Appointment of New Treasurer**

In December 2018, the Committee appointed Mrs Helen Vickers as Treasurer, following the resignation of Mr Alan Pritchard who had held the position since 2015. Mr Pritchard stepped down due to increased work commitments and was thanked by the Committee for his service. Mrs Vickers had previously served as a Committee member from 2012 to 2016 and had experience in bookkeeping for a small business in Kununurra. The appointment was ratified at the Annual General Meeting held in February 2019. The new Treasurer's first task was to oversee the transition of the organisation's accounts to a new cloud-based accounting system, which was completed in March 2019.

**18/010 – Volunteer Recognition Program**

The Committee endorsed a Volunteer Recognition Program in November 2018, to acknowledge the contribution of the organisation's volunteer base. Under the program, volunteers who complete more than 50 hours of service in a calendar year receive a certificate of appreciation and a small gift. The first awards were presented at the end of year gathering in December 2018. A total of 12 volunteers qualified for the initial round of awards. The program has been well received and will continue on an annual basis.

**19/001 – Annual General Meeting and Committee Elections**

The Annual General Meeting was held on 16 February 2019 at the Kununurra Community Hall. The meeting was attended by 23 members. The following office bearers were elected for the 2019–2020 term:

- President: Mr David Chen (re-elected)
- Vice President: Ms Sarah Thompson (re-elected)
- Secretary: Ms Margaret O'Donnell (re-elected)
- Treasurer: Mrs Helen Vickers (newly appointed, as noted above)
- Committee members: Mr Peter Nguyen, Ms Julie Brown, Mr Robert Hayes, and Ms Fiona Gallagher

The meeting also endorsed the revised financial procedures adopted by the Committee in late 2018. The minutes of the meeting were circulated to members in March 2019 and are available from the Secretariat upon request.

**19/002 – Waterbird Habitat Restoration Project – Year Two**

The second year of the Waterbird Habitat Restoration Project commenced in July 2019. The part-time project officer, Mr Daniel Wong, continued in his role. The focus for Year Two was on weed control and supplementary planting. A total of 1,200 seedlings were planted in November 2019 to replace those that had not survived the first season. The project also included a community planting day in September 2019, which attracted 15 local volunteers. A final report was submitted to the funding body in January 2020. The report noted that the project had achieved its primary objectives, including the restoration of approximately 3.5 kilometres of riparian vegetation.

**19/003 – New Field Equipment Purchases**

In March 2019, the Committee approved the purchase of new field equipment using funds remaining from the waterbird habitat grant. The purchases included two new mist nets, a pair of binoculars, and a portable GPS unit. The total cost was $3,850. The equipment was purchased from a local supplier and was added to the inventory in April 2019. The new mist nets replaced the ageing nets that had been disposed of during the office relocation in November 2018.

**19/004 – Membership Changes**

The organisation recorded a net increase in membership during the 2018–2019 financial year. As at 30 June 2019, the organisation had 87 financial members, compared with 79 at the end of the previous year. The increase was attributed to the community planting day and the waterbird habitat project, which had raised the organisation's public profile. The membership subcommittee, led by Ms Julie Brown, continued to review the membership renewal process. A reminder system was introduced in August 2019, resulting in a higher rate of on-time renewals.

**2020 Committee Meeting Minutes – Summary of Actions**

**20/001 – Appointment of New Treasurer**

At the Annual General Meeting held in November 2019, the outgoing Treasurer, Mr Peter Thompson, indicated that he would not seek re-election due to personal commitments. The Committee accepted his resignation with thanks for his service over the preceding six years. Following a call for nominations, Ms Linda Carter was elected as Treasurer effective 1 January 2020. Ms Carter holds a Bachelor of Commerce and has served on the finance subcommittee since 2017. The handover of financial records was completed on 15 January 2020, and a review of the accounts by the independent auditor was scheduled for March 2020. The Committee recorded its appreciation for Mr Thompson's diligent management of the organisation's finances.

**20/002 – Review of the Constitution**

In February 2020, the Committee established a working group to review the organisation's constitution. The review was prompted by changes to the Associations Incorporation Act and by feedback from members regarding the clarity of the rules relating to proxy voting and the election of office bearers. The working group, chaired by Ms Julie Brown, was asked to report back to the Committee by June 2020. The terms of reference included a requirement to consult with members through a survey and to propose amendments for consideration at the next Annual General Meeting. The Committee noted that any changes to the constitution would require the approval of a two-thirds majority of members present at the AGM.

**20/003 – Woodland Bird Monitoring Program – Extension**

The Woodland Bird Monitoring Program, which had been running since 2017, was extended for a further two years following a successful funding application to a philanthropic trust. The extension, announced in March 2020, secured $18,000 to support the program through to June 2022. The program involves seasonal surveys at twelve fixed sites across the region. Volunteers conduct the surveys under the supervision of the program coordinator, Dr Sarah Mitchell. The data collected are used to track trends in woodland bird populations and to inform habitat management recommendations. The funding agreement requires the submission of interim progress reports in December 2020 and December 2021, with a final report due in August 2022.

**20/004 – Office Relocation – Finalisation of Lease**

The organisation completed the relocation of its office premises in November 2018. A short-term lease on the new premises was signed at that time. In April 2020, the Committee approved the signing of a new three-year lease for the same premises, with an option to renew for a further two years. The new lease commenced on 1 May 2020. The rental amount reflects a modest increase of 3% per annum over the term of the lease. The Committee considered alternatives, including sharing premises with another conservation group, but determined that the current location provided the best balance of cost, accessibility, and storage capacity for field equipment. The lease document is held by the Secretariat.

**20/005 – Wetland Rehabilitation Project – Community Engagement**

In May 2020, the organisation commenced a community engagement component of the Wetland Rehabilitation Project. The project, which is funded by a local government grant, aims to improve the condition of a degraded wetland on the outskirts of the town. The engagement component was designed to raise awareness of the project and to recruit volunteers for planting and weed control activities. A public information session was held on 23 May 2020 and was attended by 22 residents. A project sign was installed at the wetland entrance in June 2020. The engagement activities were coordinated by Mr Daniel Wong, who was employed part-time as the project officer. Mr Wong's contract was extended to December 2020 to cover this work.
